classification.difficultyReason: Select the indicated input or output sign change, then simplify the resulting rule. The same three substitutions apply to each supplied function.

content.prompt: Write down the equation of the result when the following curves are reflected across the $x$-axis, $y$-axis, and both axes.

answer.worked:
Across the $x$-axis, negate the output.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(x)\\y&=-x^3\end{align*}$$

Across the $y$-axis, negate the input.

$$\begin{align*}y&=f(-x)\\y&=(-x)^3\\y&=-x^3\end{align*}$$

Across both axes, negate the input and the output.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(-x)\\y&=-(-x)^3\\y&=x^3\end{align*}$$

Across the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(x)\\y&=-(x-2)^2\end{align*}$$

Across the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=f(-x)\\y&=(-x-2)^2\\y&=(x+2)^2\end{align*}$$

Across both axes.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(-x)\\y&=-(-x-2)^2\\y&=-(x+2)^2\end{align*}$$

Across the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(x)\\y&=-\frac1x\end{align*}$$

Across the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=f(-x)\\y&=\frac1{-x}\\y&=-\frac1x\end{align*}$$

Across both axes.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(-x)\\y&=-\frac1{-x}\\y&=\frac1x\end{align*}$$

The denominator remains non-zero only when $x\ne0$.

Across the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(x)\\y&=-(x^2-x-2)\\y&=-x^2+x+2\end{align*}$$

Across the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=f(-x)\\y&=(-x)^2-(-x)-2\\y&=x^2+x-2\end{align*}$$

Across both axes.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(-x)\\y&=-(x^2+x-2)\\y&=-x^2-x+2\end{align*}$$

Across the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(x)\\y&=-2^x\end{align*}$$

Across the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=f(-x)\\y&=2^{-x}\end{align*}$$

Across both axes.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(-x)\\y&=-2^{-x}\end{align*}$$

Across the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(x)\\y&=-(x^3-x)\\y&=-x^3+x\end{align*}$$

Across the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y&=f(-x)\\y&=(-x)^3-(-x)\\y&=-x^3+x\end{align*}$$

Across both axes.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-f(-x)\\y&=-(-x^3+x)\\y&=x^3-x\end{align*}$$
